failedScript.narration: Five hundred and eight new homes were just approved on Lincoln's east side… and if you're thinking about selling, that number deserves your attention. A local article reports that Lincoln's City Council adopted the Parkwood development agreement on October 27—122 single-family homes and 4.2 acres of parks. That vote, together with Stardust and Stardust 12, brings the total approved to 508 homes on about 111 acres since August 2025. A development agreement freezes the rules for a set number of years—it's the last major city vote before construction paperwork begins. Right now, inventory in Lincoln is lean: 2.7 months of supply in September 2026, down from a year ago. That still favors sellers. But here's the pricing reality: homes are closing at 95% of original list price, and the average sold price sits well below the average asking price of homes currently for sale—because those are different homes. The sellers who win when new construction eventually enters the picture are the ones pricing to what buyers are actually paying today, not what listings are asking. I keep a close eye on how this development unfolds, and I'm happy to share what changes.
